Done. All 17 test cases in `markdown_test.go` pass, `gofmt` and `go vet` are clean, and the only file I touched is `markdown.go` — no new files, no test modifications. ## What I did The original `Render` was a single byte-at-a-time loop with a tangle of flags (`header`, `he`, `list`, `listOpened`) and index arithmetic, where block state leaked across lines and closing tags were deferred to the end of the document. I rewrote it as a line-oriented parser: - **`Render`** — splits the input on `\n` and renders each line independently via a `switch` on its prefix: - `#…` → `renderHeader` - `* …` → list item, with the only cross-line state being `inList` (opens `
    ` on the first item, closes it when the list ends or the input finishes) - anything else → `

    …

    ` - blank lines close an open list but emit nothing - **`renderEmphasis`** — the `__`/`_` → ``/`` replacements, factored out of the main loop (same `strings.Replace(…, 1)` semantics as the original, now applied per line) - **`renderHeader`** — counts leading `#`s: 1–6 → `…`; 7+ → a paragraph with the hashes kept as literal text (the original's "h7 is a paragraph" behavior) The refactor notes are captured in the doc comment on `Render`, per the spec's suggestion. One bug fixed along the way: the original deferred the h7 paragraph's `

    ` to document end, which my per-line rendering now closes correctly within the line (that's what the `h7_header_level_is_a_paragraph` test caught on the first run).
